per_question.question: Are there quantity limits on prescription drugs under NC Medicaid, and when is prior authorization required for pharmacy claims?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. Under **NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 9**, NC Medicaid may impose **quantity limitations for episodic drugs**. The surfaced policy text says this in the section on **“Quantity and Episodic Drugs,”** which also addresses **prior authorization criteria and requirements**. The surfaced evidence does **not** give specific current numeric quantity limits, so I cannot verify dollar amounts, day-supply numbers, or other exact thresholds from the text retrieved here. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment) (Policy 9, § 5.4; § 5.4.3, effective 2024-07-15; current authoritative document per amendment check)

## When prior authorization is required for pharmacy claims

Prior authorization is required for the **drugs or drug categories listed in NC Medicaid’s pharmacy prior-approval criteria**. In the surfaced Policy 9 material, the **“Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria”** section lists the products/categories subject to prior approval, and **Attachment K** is identified as **“Pharmacy Prior Approval Criteria.”** [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment) (Policy 9, “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria”; Attachment K, effective 2024-07-15; current authoritative document per amendment check)

Examples named in the surfaced prior-approval list include:
- GLP-1 receptor agonists and combinations
- Growth hormones
- Hepatitis C medications
- Opioid analgesics
- PCSK9 inhibitors
- Triptans
- Synagis
- Therapeutic continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGM) and related supplies
- Various named drugs and specialty categories such as Aduhelm, Camzyos, Epidiolex, Evrysdi, Lequembi, and Zolgensma  
[Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment) (Policy 9, “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria,” effective 2024-07-15; current authoritative document per amendment check)

## Bottom line

- **Quantity limits:** **Yes**, NC Medicaid may apply quantity limits for episodic drugs. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment) (Policy 9, § 5.4.3)
- **Prior authorization:** Required when the claim is for a drug/category included in NC Medicaid’s **pharmacy prior-approval criteria**. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment) (Policy 9, “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria”; Attachment K)

If you want, I can next help identify whether a **specific medication** is on NC Medicaid’s prior-approval list.
